title: Route sacred_window_repository.dart through the sacred_time barrel instead of deep cross-feature imports (Rule 2)

evidence.quote: match($1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print

why: features/notifications reaches directly into features/sacred_time's domain internals instead of features/sacred_time/sacred_time.dart (itself an empty stub barrel with no exports), so a refactor inside sacred_time's domain layer can silently break notification scheduling with no barrel-boundary warning. Separately, make audit check 15's awk pattern always compares a feature name against itself: it runs match() against $0 (the whole grep -rn line, which starts with the FILE PATH), so the first 'features/X/' match in $0 is always the same X captured from $1 -- a[1] and b[1] can never differ, so check 15 can never print a warning for ANY file. This is confirmed empirically: check 15 produced zero WARN output in the clean-tree baseline despite this real cross-feature import existing.
recommendation: Populate features/sacred_time/sacred_time.dart with the needed exports (SacredLocation, SacredWindow, ZmanimWindowService) and import through it; separately fix the Makefile check 15 awk pattern to extract the import path (not the full grep line) before comparing feature names.
acceptance_criteria: make audit check 15, once its awk bug is fixed, flags this file today and reports clean after the barrel fix is applied.

corrections: Third evidence item cites 'learning_tracker/learning_tracker/Makefile:380' -- that path doesn't exist (double-nested). Real file is learning_tracker/Makefile; the quoted awk pattern appears verbatim at lines 378 and 384, not 380 (380 is the 'WARN: the following files...' echo). Also, the recommendation to populate/import via features/sacred_time/sacred_time.dart conflicts with current coding-standards.md Rule 2, which names lib/features/Y/providers.dart (not yet existing for any feature) as the only sanctioned barrel.
